references.text: Luke 14:7-11 speaks about choosing the least honorable seats at a wedding feast, reflecting Jesus' teaching on humility and warning against seeking the highest places of honor, as in Matthew 23:6.

Mark 12:38-40 criticizes the scribes for their desire to walk around in long robes, seek greetings in the marketplaces, have the best seats in the synagogues, and take places of honor at meals, parallel to Matthew 23:6.
Matthew 20:20-28 discusses the request to sit at Jesus' right and left hand in his kingdom, reflecting the theme of seeking positions of honor that is criticized in Matthew 23:6.

John 3:1-9, where Nicodemus, a Pharisee, comes to Jesus by night, can be indirectly related to the behavior of the Pharisees criticized in Matthew 23:6, even though it does not directly mention seeking places of honor.
